title: Integration baseline and standalone test workflow
label: A dependable foundation
benefit: A repeatable starting point and checks that catch problems as the app grows.
description: Inspect PR #1 and the current remotes/branch. Record the baseline commit and startup commands, create or identify a small residential fixture, and isolate the missing TakeoffCraft test dependency so standalone checks report an explicit skip or run a focused equivalent. Do not fabricate passing external checks or merge the PR without user authorization. Done: clean startup and documented reproducible test commands on a fresh development checkout; no accidental use of upstream-only main.
note: Integrated with the original wall, material and dimension prototype.
currentCapability: Standalone integration foundation and the original wall/material/dimension prototype are adopted.
nextWork: Maintain reproducible isolated startup and explicit sibling availability notices; no new F01 implementation needed.

title: Precision, references and migration contract
label: Measurements you can trust
benefit: Protect measurements, wall details and references through edits and saving.
description: Document length/angle units, geometry tolerances, display rounding, local/project coordinates, supported file versions and named-reference behavior. Add fixtures for imperial/metric units, translated coordinates, tiny offsets, curves and repeated edit/save/reopen. Define safe handling for unknown schema versions and broken hosts. Done: tests prove supported operations meet the agreed tolerance and fail visibly outside it. Use the existing 0.005 mm regression threshold as a starting test bound, not as a claim of universal CAD-kernel accuracy.
note: Validated within documented fixtures; not a universal accuracy guarantee.
currentCapability: Numeric/reference/version contracts and repeated persistence fixtures are adopted. Six wall references, stable identities and unknown-record protection are usable.
nextWork: Extend known schema/migration contracts for future layer priority, join modes, copy/reference policies and constraints. Fixture precision is not a universal accuracy warranty.

title: Performance baseline and profiling harness
label: Know where the app slows down
benefit: Measure everyday tasks so future speed improvements target real problems.
description: Measure cold/warm open, selection, pan/zoom, wall/type edits, roof regeneration, save and PDF generation on small/medium/large residential fixtures. Record hardware, browser/runtime, fixture sizes, p50/p95 and memory. Proposed starting UX targets for a typical house: selection/Properties feedback within 100 ms, interactive preview frames within 33 ms, and common committed edits within 500 ms at p95. Validate or revise these targets using measured baseline data. Done: reproducible timings identify the dominant cost and separate geometry work from UI/IFC parsing/serialization.
note: Measurement tools are complete. This feature does not itself make the app faster.
currentCapability: Performance harness/profiling is adopted. Exact-main CI collected900 browser observations in30 groups, zero source errors.
nextWork: Address measured responsiveness and CI-duration follow-ups. The27 model timing groups are unmeasured in this browser-only artifact; benchmark completion is not a speed improvement.

title: Layered plan graphics and vector output

benefit: Show framing, finishes, air gaps and membranes in plans and printed drawings.
description: Render authored wall layers with project fills/colors, unfilled cavities, and membrane boundary lines. Offer useful coarse/medium/fine detail behavior. Start with straight unjoined walls; then cover curves, junction clipping and opening cuts before declaring the card complete. Screen and vector PDF/sheets must share the same layer boundaries. Done: a material-style edit changes graphics without changing geometry; walls with openings and corners remain legible and exports retain scale. Excludes per-layer 3D solids.
note: Accepted drawing scope is integrated. Fine-view responsiveness remains an open follow-up.
currentCapability: Layered plan graphics, cavities, membrane lines, detail settings and vector consistency are adopted for accepted scope. View Range exists.
nextWork: F04-B range/RCP edge-case evidence; coordinate new join ownership with F08-B. Fine-view responsiveness and crowded short labels stay open.

title: 3D wall assemblies and framing coordination
label: Draw walls and coordinate their framing
benefit: Sketch walls in 3D, reveal their framing and fit outlets and shower niches around modeled studs and clear bays.
deps: F02/F03 and existing assemblies; agreed F09 input contracts; focused framing/host audit coordinated with F08, F15 and F24. Discovery before implementation.
description:
Keep one logical wall as the source of truth for layers, core, orientation, openings and derived framing. Audit and extend existing framing and reveal tools first. Configure representative member sizes, spacing, origin, plates and opening rules; derive inspectable members and clear bays deterministically. Preserve placement intent, valid identities and compatible overrides; report missing/split bays and conflicts rather than leaving stale geometry.

Proposed first proof: one straight vertical timber wall sketched in 3D, one rectangular opening, generated framing, one outlet and one shower niche. Check box/clearance and niche width/height/depth envelopes; no silent stud cutting. Finished/core/framing views use the same model. Edits, Undo/Redo and save/reopen preserve relationships or explain conflicts. Manual and semantic MCP actions share validation and operations.

Stage richer overrides, assembly switching, supported junctions, scoped review/field-verification records and project-scale performance after the proof. Engineered sizing, fabrication, automatic quantities, full MEP routing, broad building systems and advanced animated reveals are outside the initial slice. Generated framing is design/coordination information with explicit assumptions, not automatic field or compliance verification.
